Key points
• Phosphorus main functions include bone formation, regulation of gene transcription, enzymes activation, energy
production and storage (ATP), blood buffer in extracellular ﬂuids, and cellular signal transduction.
• The main dietary sources of phosphorus are high protein foods, dietary supplements, fortiﬁed food/water, and phosphorus
added during food processing.
• Absorption has two main pathways: a sodium-dependent transcellular pathway, and the predominant sodium-
independent paracellular pathway.
• Phosphorus is tightly regulated and homeostasis is maintained by the intestine, the kidney and the bone, and the activity of
three hormones: parathyroid hormone (PTH), calcitriol and ﬁbroblast growth factor 23 (FGF-23).
